deck_title: Taubin implicit curve first-order gradient normalization vs naive algebraic stroke thinning rig

cards.subtitle: Deterministic Gabriel Taubin (ACM TOG 1994) first-order implicit curve Euclidean distance approximation (d_Taubin = |f(x,y)| / ||grad f(x,y)||, dividing out the boundary gradient norm ||grad f|| = 2R on f(x,y) = x^2 + y^2 - R^2 = 0 to lock uniform stroke thickness W = 1.0000x across 17 radius stations R in [0.50, 4.50]) versus naive raw algebraic thresholding (|f(x,y)| < w, which thins the rendered stroke width as 1/(2R) down to 0.3333x at R=1.50, 0.2000x at R=2.50, and 0.1111x at R=4.50 across 16/17 stations) and 64-step closest-point curve projection.
